About

# About Zemanium.

Zemanium is a geothermal invention lab. We design the instruments, well hardware and models that hot wells need, test them in simulation against rules we fix beforehand, and publish what comes out.

01 / Facts

## The basics.

| Name | Zemanium (zeh-MAY-nee-um) |
|---|---|
| Founded | 2026 |
| Founder | Toni Zemani |
| Field | Enhanced and superhot geothermal: well integrity, flow control, sensing, power conversion and cost modelling |
| Stage | Simulation campaigns run on the first programmes; models, forecasts, records and drawings published; physical test campaigns next |
| Contact | [toni@zemanium.com](mailto:toni@zemanium.com) |
| Website | https://zemanium.com/ |

02 / Mission

## Make Earth's heat the world's power.

Our mission is to make geothermal the world's dominant energy source. Heat under our feet is available day and night in every country, and the obstacle is cost. We work on the equipment that decides that cost: wells that survive, flow that reaches the hot rock, instruments that keep working, and plants that convert more of the heat.

Our development target is firm geothermal power at $30 to $45 per megawatt-hour. The [cost guide](https://zemanium.com/guides/geothermal-electricity-cost) shows what a plant has to cost to get there.

03 / Method

## How we work.

1. Every invention goes through a simulated test campaign before any metal is cut. We write down the mechanism, the equations, the pass and fail rules and the conditions that would prove us wrong, and then we run it.
2. The rules that judge a simulation are the rules that will judge the bench test.
3. Every number carries a label: measured, vendor-stated, SIMULATED, assumption. A simulated result is never called a qualification.

04 / Record

## The record so far.

| Date | What | Where |
|---|---|---|
| 5 October 2026 | Power-cost model: 1,080 scenarios and a 2,000-draw financial stress test | [Live model](https://zemanium.com/confidence/) |
| 5 October 2026 | Release demonstrator drawings and a commanded-release model, run through 48 simulated campaigns | [Dossier](https://zemanium.com/docs/04-technical-dossier#shift) |
| 8 October 2026 | Sensor readout software: maximum temperature error cut from 131.178 K to 1.240 K on the same simulated signals | [Research](https://zemanium.com/room/#sensing) |
| 19 November 2026 | Forecasts of the Project Red well pair registered and time-stamped. The model matches the Nevada regulator's record to 0.51 °F on nine steady months | [Forecast and audit record](https://github.com/tonizemani2/forecast-audit) |
| 20 November 2026 | Three sourced guides and this open catalogue | [Guides](https://zemanium.com/guides/), [Open data](https://zemanium.com/open/) |
| 24 November 2026 | Fervo Project Red tracker, guides to geothermal stocks, renewability and firm power, open data files and an MCP server for AI agents | [Tracker](https://zemanium.com/fervo-project-red), [Guides](https://zemanium.com/guides/) |

All model results are SIMULATED.

05 / Contact

## Get in touch.

We are hiring engineers to lead physical test campaigns, working with operators and manufacturers on hot-well problems, and building with investors who back hardware. Write to [toni@zemanium.com](mailto:toni@zemanium.com) and say what you need to decide. The [open research page](https://zemanium.com/open/#work) lists the kinds of work we take on.

Tracker · Toni Zemani · updated 24 November 2026

# Fervo Project Red: the monthly record against our registered forecast.

Project Red, Fervo Energy's pilot well pair in Nevada, produced 316 °F at the wellhead in July 2026, down from a 347 °F plateau in 2024, according to the Nevada regulator's monthly record. We registered a forecast for every month to December 2027 and score it here as each new month is published.

Monthly values are measured and operator-reported to the Nevada Division of Minerals, copied without changes. The forecast is [MODEL], frozen and time-stamped on 19 November 2026. Independent analysis from public records; not investment advice. Zemanium holds no position in any security.

01 / Record

## What the regulator's record shows.

The producing well delivered 343 to 347 °F through most of 2024 and 2025. From December 2025 the monthly mean fell every month: 342, 341, 338, 336, 334 and 332 °F in May 2026. June read 242 °F in a month with 32% less production, and July read 316 °F.

![Line chart of Project Red's monthly wellhead temperature from December 2023 to July 2026, followed by the shaded forecast band to December 2027](https://zemanium.com/assets/charts/project-red-record.svg)

Chart free to reuse under CC BY 4.0 with credit to Zemanium. Months under 1 million gallons or below 230 °F are left off the line and kept in the table and data file.

| Month | Wellhead temperature | Produced, million gallons | Injection temperature |
|---|---|---|---|
| Aug 2025 | 345 °F | 19.8 | 174 °F |
| Sep 2025 | 115 °F | 6.4 | 58 °F |
| Oct 2025 | 320 °F | 20.6 | 171 °F |
| Nov 2025 | 344 °F | 24.4 | 170 °F |
| Dec 2025 | 342 °F | 25.6 | 171 °F |
| Jan 2026 | 341 °F | 25.7 | 171 °F |
| Feb 2026 | 338 °F | 24.0 | 172 °F |
| Mar 2026 | 336 °F | 25.8 | 168 °F |
| Apr 2026 | 334 °F | 25.0 | 86 °F |
| May 2026 | 332 °F | 26.7 | 92 °F |
| Jun 2026 | 242 °F | 18.2 | 75 °F |
| Jul 2026 | 316 °F | 22.8 | 86 °F |

The temperature of the water sent back down changed in April 2026, from about 170 °F to between 75 and 92 °F. Colder injection cools the fractures faster, so our forecast uses the cold-reinjection case from that month on.

02 / Forecast

## What we forecast, and when it was fixed.

We fitted a conduction model of the fractured rock to nine steady months. It matches them with a root-mean-square error of 0.51 °F. Twenty-one model runs of 1,440 met that fit, and their spread sets the band. The forecast files were hashed and time-stamped by two independent authorities on 19 November 2026, before any of the forecast months were published.

- December 2026: median 318.1 °F, band 312.0 to 324.6 °F.
- July 2027: median 298.0 °F, band 286.9 to 310.6 °F.
- December 2027: median 284.6 °F, band 265.8 to 300.0 °F.

The model also says how much of the stated fracture area exchanges heat: 32% to 63% across the accepted runs. That figure decides how long a well pair of this design stays hot.

03 / Score

## Score so far.

Each month is scored on the 7th after the regulator publishes it. The latest workbook, dated 29 September 2026, runs to July 2026, so the first forecast month is still to come.

| Month | Forecast median | Band | Regulator value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Aug 2026 | 328.1 °F | 324.2 to 332.6 °F | next regulator workbook |
| Sep 2026 | 325.5 °F | 321.2 to 330.5 °F | next regulator workbook |
| Oct 2026 | 323.0 °F | 318.2 to 328.5 °F | next regulator workbook |
| Nov 2026 | 320.6 °F | 315.2 to 326.6 °F | next regulator workbook |
| Dec 2026 | 318.1 °F | 312.0 to 324.6 °F | next regulator workbook |

04 / Water

## How much water comes back.

Over 18 steady months, 72.7% of the injected volume came back up the producer, or 65.9% by mass. The ratio has not moved in 2.3 years: +0.2 points a year, plus or minus 1.5. Since December 2023 the pair took in 192.9 million gallons more than it returned.

05 / Questions

## Common questions.

### What is Fervo Project Red?

Project Red is Fervo Energy's first enhanced geothermal well pair, drilled at Blue Mountain in Humboldt County, Nevada. Its monthly production and injection are reported to the Nevada Division of Minerals under permits 1505 and 1506, which makes it the only enhanced geothermal production history in the public record.

### Is Project Red cooling down?

Yes, on the regulator's monthly wellhead metric. The record held 344 to 347 °F in steady months from May 2024 to November 2025 and read 332 °F in May 2026 and 316 °F in July 2026.

### Why is Fervo stock down?

Fervo Energy listed on Nasdaq as FRVO on 13 May 2026 after pricing its offering at $27 a share. A short seller report published in 2026 cited Project Red's temperature and water record. We checked 33 public claims about the well pair, from the short seller, the company and others, against the regulator's data; the audit is public and each verdict follows a written rule.

### What does Project Red mean for Cape Station?

Cape Station in Utah uses a later well design at larger scale and reached first power on 24 September 2026, by the company's account. Project Red is the only well pair with a public monthly record, so it is the best public evidence for how fast this kind of reservoir cools. Our forecast F5 covers a Cape-class producer.

### When is the next update?

On the 7th of each month after the Nevada Division of Minerals publishes a new workbook. Each update adds the new months to the chart and scores them against the registered band.

06 / Data

## Data and tools for people and agents.

- [Project Red monthly record (JSON)](https://zemanium.com/data/project-red-monthly.json) and [registered forecast (JSON)](https://zemanium.com/data/project-red-forecast.json). CC BY 4.0.
- MCP server for AI agents: `https://zemanium.com/mcp`. Tools return the record, the forecast, Nevada plant output and geothermal cost cases.

- [Geothermal stocks](https://zemanium.com/guides/geothermal-stocks): every listed producer, with the Nevada plant record.

Need a scorecard for another project? Write to [toni@zemanium.com](mailto:toni@zemanium.com).

Guide · Toni Zemani · 20 November 2026

# Enhanced geothermal systems: how they work and what limits them.

An enhanced geothermal system (EGS) makes a geothermal reservoir where nature left hot rock without enough water or cracks. Engineers drill into the rock, open fractures in it, and circulate water through them to carry the heat to a power plant.

Figures from companies are their own statements. Figures marked SIMULATED come from Zemanium's models. The field data we show from Utah FORGE was measured and published by others.

01 / In brief

## The short answer.

- Conventional geothermal needs heat, water and permeable rock in the same place. EGS needs only the heat and supplies the other two.
- Fervo Energy's Cape Station in Utah produced first power on 24 September 2026 from a unit of about 33 MW, by the company's account.
- Today's equipment keeps EGS to about 220 °C and about 10 megawatts of electricity per production well, according to ARPA-E.
- The open engineering problems are keeping the reservoir hot for decades, spreading flow evenly through the fractures, building wells that survive, and cost.

02 / Mechanism

## How an enhanced geothermal system works.

1. Drill an injection well into hot, mostly dry rock. Modern projects turn the well horizontal at depth, as shale drillers do.
2. Pump water down under controlled pressure. It opens new fractures and reopens old ones, which gives the rock the permeability it lacked.
3. Drill a production well through the fractured zone, parallel to the first.
4. Circulate water from one well to the other. It heats up as it crosses the fractures.
5. Bring the hot water to the surface, pass its heat to a power plant, and inject the cooled water again.

The water runs in a loop, so the plant delivers power around the clock in any weather. The US Department of Energy also counts two related approaches as next-generation geothermal. Closed-loop systems circulate fluid through sealed pipes in the rock and use no fractures. [Superhot systems](https://zemanium.com/guides/superhot-rock-geothermal) go after rock above 375 °C.

03 / Status

## Where the technology stands in 2026.

| Milestone | Figure | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| First power at Cape Station, Utah | 24 September 2026, first unit about 33 MW; first phase planned at about 100 MW | company statement |
| Production well test at Cape Station | about 195 °C, 8 to 10 MW of electricity sustained per production well, flow of 107 kg/s over 30 days | operator preprint |
| Drilling speed, Sawtooth 7 well | 19,448 ft measured depth with a 7,500 ft lateral in 21 days, in rock at about 238 °C | company statement, July 2026 |
| Newberry, Oregon | a well at 331 °C in October 2025 | press report of company statement |
| Public research site | Utah FORGE, funded by the Department of Energy, publishes its well and stimulation data | Department of Energy |

Earlier Department of Energy demonstrations ran at Newberry Volcano, The Geysers, Brady, Desert Peak and Raft River.

04 / Limits

## Four limits engineers are working on.

### Thermal decline

Injected water is cold. It cools the fracture faces first and the rock behind them more slowly. If most of the flow takes a few short paths, those paths cool within years and the produced temperature drops. How much fracture area the water touches decides how long a well pair lasts. ARPA-E's goal for superhot reservoirs is heat extraction for at least ten years without significant decline.

### Uneven flow

Fractures do not share flow equally. In one published Utah FORGE production log, the interpretation could not resolve how inflow was distributed below 9,240 ft and reported it as a single aggregate. You can [inspect that profile](https://zemanium.com/confidence/#field) in our field replay. The Department of Energy funds work on reversible ways to change fracture permeability for this reason.

### Wells that survive

Casing and cement expand when the well heats and contract when cold water goes down. The Department of Energy says the tools sold for checking cement and casing suit the hot end of oil and gas but are generally inadequate for hotter geothermal wells. Casing and cementing make up 30% to 40% or more of a well's cost.

### Cost

The Department of Energy target is $45 per megawatt-hour by 2035. Our guide to [geothermal electricity cost](https://zemanium.com/guides/geothermal-electricity-cost) shows which inputs move that number.

05 / Tools

## Public data and tools.

- [Reservoir explorer](https://zemanium.com/demo/): a 3D model where you change flow, well spacing and rock temperature and watch thermal decline and pumping respond. SIMULATED, illustrative.
- [Utah FORGE field replay](https://zemanium.com/confidence/#field): 518 rows of a published production-log interpretation by SLB and the University of Utah, with attribution and the gaps left visible. CC BY 4.0, DOI 10.15121/2473673.
- [Power-cost model](https://zemanium.com/confidence/): the cost per megawatt-hour of a simulated EGS plant under your assumptions.

We build models and hardware for this problem and review forecasts for others. Write to [toni@zemanium.com](mailto:toni@zemanium.com).

06 / Questions

## Common questions.

### What does EGS stand for?

Enhanced geothermal system. It is a geothermal reservoir made by engineering: wells are drilled into hot rock, fractures are opened to let water through, and the water carries heat to a power plant.

### How is EGS different from conventional geothermal?

A conventional geothermal plant sits on a natural hydrothermal system, where hot rock, water and permeability already exist together. An enhanced geothermal system starts with hot rock only and adds the water and the permeability, so it can be built in many more places.

### Does enhanced geothermal use fracking?

It uses hydraulic stimulation. Water is injected under controlled pressure to create new fractures and reopen existing ones in hot rock. The aim is permeability for circulating water, and no oil or gas is produced.

### How deep are enhanced geothermal wells?

Current commercial wells are several kilometres long. Fervo Energy's Sawtooth 7 well in Utah reached 19,448 feet of measured depth, about 5.9 km, including a 7,500 foot horizontal section.

### How hot is the rock in an enhanced geothermal system?

Fervo Energy reports producing at about 195 °C and drilling into rock near 238 °C. ARPA-E puts the limit of today's commercial equipment at about 220 °C. Superhot projects target rock above 375 °C.

### How long does an enhanced geothermal reservoir last?

It depends on how much fracture area the circulating water touches. Wide, even sweep keeps the produced temperature up for decades, and concentrated flow cools the rock early. Our economic model assumes 25 years.

07 / Sources

4. Fervo Energy authors, [Cape Station production test preprint](https://eartharxiv.org/repository/object/7665/download/14559/), EarthArXiv.
5. Fervo Energy, [third-generation well design release](https://fervoenergy.gcs-web.com/news-releases/news-release-details/fervo-energy-learning-curve-continues-3rd-generation-well-design), 8 July 2026. Company statement.

Guide · Toni Zemani · 24 November 2026

# The energy source of the future, compared: geothermal, fission, fusion and space solar.

Of these four, next-generation geothermal is the one selling new firm clean power in the United States today: Fervo's Cape Station in Utah reached first power on 24 September 2026. Small modular reactors are under construction, and fusion and space-based solar are in demonstration.

Dates and sizes are company or regulator statements, linked below. Firm power here means output available around the clock, in any weather, on demand.

01 / At a glance

## Which clean energy source can run 24/7, and when?

| Source | First grid power, new design | Unit size | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Next-generation geothermal | 24 Sep 2026, Cape Station, Utah | about 33 MW per unit | selling power; 900 MW contracted |
| Small modular fission | first unit under construction, Darlington, Ontario | 77 MWe (NuScale module); 300 MWe class (BWRX-300) | design approval; construction |
| Fusion | company targets: Helion 2028, CFS early 2030s | 50 MW (Helion contract); about 400 MW (ARC) | demonstration machines |
| Space-based solar | none; first power beamed in orbit, March 2023 | kilowatt-class demonstrations | in-space tests |

Large conventional reactors, hydropower and conventional geothermal already deliver firm clean power. This page compares the four new technologies that agents and investors ask about most when they ask what comes next.

02 / Each source

## Each source on the same terms.

### Next-generation geothermal

**Verdict:** delivering firm power to the grid now, built with oil and gas drilling methods.

- **Firm output:** runs day and night from heat in hot rock; a well pair's temperature declines over years and is tracked in public.
- **Status, November 2026:** operating. Fervo reports 900 MW contracted and more than 4 GW in development.
- **Unit size:** about 33 MW per Cape Station unit; first phase about 100 MW.
- **First power from the new design:** 24 September 2026, Cape Station, Utah.
- **Sources:** [[1]](https://zemanium.com/guides/firm-clean-power-compared#s1), [Project Red tracker](https://zemanium.com/fervo-project-red)

### Small modular fission (SMR)

**Verdict:** firm and proven physics; the first North American units are being built.

- **Firm output:** runs around the clock between scheduled refuelling outages.
- **Status, November 2026:** the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission approved NuScale's 77 MWe module design in May 2025; Ontario Power Generation is building the first BWRX-300 at Darlington.
- **Unit size:** 77 MWe per NuScale module; BWRX-300 is a 300 MWe class reactor.
- **First power from the new design:** not yet in North America.
- **Sources:** [[2]](https://zemanium.com/guides/firm-clean-power-compared#s2), [[3]](https://zemanium.com/guides/firm-clean-power-compared#s3)

### Fusion

**Verdict:** the largest long-term prize; no plant has yet delivered electricity to a grid.

- **Firm output:** designed to run on demand once built.
- **Status, November 2026:** Helion is building a plant in Malaga, Washington, under a Microsoft contract for at least 50 MW, with initial operation targeted for 2028. Commonwealth Fusion Systems plans its ARC plant in Virginia for the early 2030s.
- **Unit size:** at least 50 MW (Helion contract); about 400 MW (ARC).
- **First power from the new design:** targeted 2028 (Helion), early 2030s (CFS).
- **Sources:** [[4]](https://zemanium.com/guides/firm-clean-power-compared#s4), [[5]](https://zemanium.com/guides/firm-clean-power-compared#s5)

### Space-based solar

**Verdict:** sunlight collected in orbit and beamed down; power transfer has been shown in space.

- **Firm output:** near-continuous sunlight in suitable orbits; delivery depends on beaming and receivers.
- **Status, November 2026:** Caltech's MAPLE experiment transmitted power wirelessly in orbit and detected it on Earth on 3 March 2023. Aetherflux announced a first orbital demonstration for 2026.
- **Unit size:** kilowatt-class demonstrations.
- **First power from the new design:** no grid power yet.
- **Sources:** [[6]](https://zemanium.com/guides/firm-clean-power-compared#s6), [[7]](https://zemanium.com/guides/firm-clean-power-compared#s7)

03 / Buyers

## Who is buying firm clean power for data centers?

- Google and NV Energy: 115 MW of enhanced geothermal from Fervo's Corsac Station under Nevada's Clean Transition Tariff [[8]](https://zemanium.com/guides/firm-clean-power-compared#s8).
- Google and NV Energy: a geothermal portfolio contract with Ormat for up to 150 MW, signed in 2026 [[9]](https://zemanium.com/guides/firm-clean-power-compared#s9).
- Microsoft and Helion: at least 50 MW of fusion power from 2028, under a 2023 agreement [[4]](https://zemanium.com/guides/firm-clean-power-compared#s4).

Geothermal is the one of the three with plants already producing. We publish the operating record and forecasts that buyers and lenders use to judge how long that output lasts: [listed producers](https://zemanium.com/guides/geothermal-stocks), [the Project Red tracker](https://zemanium.com/fervo-project-red) and [cost per megawatt-hour](https://zemanium.com/guides/geothermal-electricity-cost).

04 / Questions

## Common questions.

### What is the best energy source for the future?

For firm clean power that can be contracted this decade, next-generation geothermal and fission are the two technologies with plants built or under construction. Geothermal delivered its first next-generation grid power in September 2026; fusion and space-based solar are still in demonstration.

### Is geothermal better than nuclear?

They serve the same need, power around the clock. Geothermal needs hot rock, burns no fuel and uses drilling methods from oil and gas; fission plants can be sited in more places. New geothermal is producing power in the United States today, while the first North American SMR is under construction.

### Geothermal vs fusion: which comes first?

Geothermal. Next-generation geothermal reached first grid power in September 2026. The first fusion power plants are targeted for 2028 (Helion) and the early 2030s (Commonwealth Fusion Systems).

### What is space-based solar power?

Solar panels in orbit collect sunlight and beam the energy to receivers on the ground. Caltech demonstrated wireless power transfer in space in March 2023, and no system yet supplies a grid.

Guide · Toni Zemani · 20 November 2026

# What geothermal electricity costs, and what sets the price.

A geothermal plant is paid for almost entirely before it produces anything. The cost of each megawatt-hour then depends on four things: what the wells cost, how much power each well delivers, how long that output lasts, and the interest rate on the money.

Numbers marked SIMULATED come from our own model and are scenarios built on assumptions. They are requirements for a design, and no plant has been built to them. Numbers from other organisations are quoted with their source.

01 / In brief

## The short answer.

- The US Department of Energy wants enhanced geothermal power at $45 per megawatt-hour by 2035. It describes that as a cut of about 90% from where the technology stood in 2022.
- ARPA-E's SUPERHOT program aims lower for wells above 375 °C: under $30 per megawatt-hour by 2040.
- In our own model the same simulated plant costs $83.02, $43.35 or $35.00 per megawatt-hour depending on its capital cost and discount rate. The rock and the wells are identical in all three cases.
- Zemanium's development target is $30 to $45 per megawatt-hour. It is what our hardware program is designed toward.

02 / Method

## How LCOE is calculated.

The levelized cost of electricity (LCOE) is the price per megawatt-hour at which a plant pays back everything spent on it over its life, including the return its lenders and owners expect. It divides discounted lifetime cost by discounted lifetime output:

`LCOE = sum of (cost in year t / (1 + r)^t) / sum of (electricity exported in year t / (1 + r)^t)`

Here `r` is the discount rate and `t` runs from construction to the last operating year. For geothermal the largest costs fall in year zero: drilling, completing the wells and building the power plant. Fuel is free. That makes the answer sensitive to the discount rate and to how long the wells keep their output.

Use exported electricity in the denominator. A geothermal plant spends some of its own output on pumps and auxiliaries, and an LCOE computed on gross generation flatters the plant. Our model exports gross generation minus pumping minus 5% of gross for auxiliaries.

03 / Targets

## Published cost targets.

| Who | Target | By | Applies to |
|---|---|---|---|
| US Department of Energy, Enhanced Geothermal Shot | $45/MWh | 2035 | enhanced geothermal systems |
| ARPA-E, SUPERHOT program | under $30/MWh | 2040 | reservoirs above 375 °C and 22 MPa, 10 to 20 GW |
| Zemanium | $30 to $45/MWh | development target, no date claimed | our hardware and well program |

The analysis behind the Department of Energy figure put developed deep enhanced geothermal at $45.60 per megawatt-hour in 2035, rounded to $45. All three rows are goals.

04 / Worked example

## One simulated plant, three prices.

Our power-cost model holds the physics fixed and changes only the money. The reservoir starts at 200 °C, runs for 25 simulated years, and feeds a plant sized to its peak output of 28.322 MW gross.

| Case | Capital assumptions | Real discount rate | LCOE |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reference | reference plant and well costs | 8% | $83.02/MWh |
| Target package | $1,500 per gross kW plant, $15m subsurface, $3m other | 8% | $43.35/MWh |
| Target package, cheaper money | same | 4% | $35.00/MWh |

SIMULATED · assumption scenarios · 5 October 2026

Halving the cost of capital takes $8.35 off each megawatt-hour without touching a single piece of equipment. Getting from $83.02 to $43.35 needs the plant and the wells to cost roughly what the target package says. No supplier has quoted those prices. They tell us what our hardware has to achieve.

The model runs 1,080 cost scenarios on output trajectories from GEOPHIRES-X 3.18.3, the open source simulator from NREL. It charges 2% of installed capital a year for operations, make-up water and $8 per exported megawatt-hour, books a $5m event in year 12 and $2m in year 25, and assumes the plant runs 90% of the time. A stress test draws 2,000 combinations of discount rate (4% to 12%), capital overrun (0.8 to 1.2 times) and a mid-life replacement of up to $10m.

05 / Drivers

## What moves the cost.

### Wells

The Department of Energy calls lower well construction cost a requirement for expanding enhanced geothermal, and puts casing and cementing alone at 30% to 40% or more of what a well costs. Drilling time is falling: Fervo Energy reports reaching 19,448 feet of measured depth in 21 days on its Sawtooth 7 well in July 2026.

### Power per well

A well that produces twice the power halves the drilling bill per megawatt. ARPA-E says today's equipment limits enhanced geothermal to about 220 °C and about 10 megawatts of electricity per production well, and that wells above 375 °C could reach 30 to 50. That gap is why developers want [superhot rock](https://zemanium.com/guides/superhot-rock-geothermal).

### How long the output lasts

Cold water injected into hot rock cools the rock it touches. If the water sweeps a small volume, the produced temperature falls early and every later year earns less. Our model includes a case that fails this way: with the reservoir volume cut from 1 cubic kilometre to 0.014, the plant ends up importing power, and we publish no price for it.

### Cost of capital

Because nearly all spending comes first, the discount rate acts on the whole bill. The example above moves 19% between 8% and 4%.

### The plant on the surface

Hotter fluid converts a larger share of its heat to electricity, so a 200 °C plant needs more equipment per kilowatt than a hotter one. The model lets you set installed plant cost from $1,500 to $4,500 per gross kilowatt.

06 / Tool

## Run the model yourself.

The [power-cost model](https://zemanium.com/confidence/) runs in your browser with no account. Set the plant cost, subsurface cost, discount rate and a target price, and it returns the LCOE and the capital the design can afford. It also shows the cases that fail. The 3D [reservoir explorer](https://zemanium.com/demo/) shows how flow, well spacing and rock temperature change thermal decline and pumping.

If you want this analysis for a specific project, or an independent review of a forecast, write to [toni@zemanium.com](mailto:toni@zemanium.com).

07 / Questions

## Common questions.

### Is geothermal energy expensive?

It is expensive to build and cheap to run. Almost all of the cost is drilling and plant construction paid up front, so the price per megawatt-hour depends on well cost, output per well, how long that output lasts and the interest rate. The US Department of Energy target for enhanced geothermal is $45 per megawatt-hour by 2035.

### How is the LCOE of a geothermal plant calculated?

Add up every cost over the plant's life, discount each year's cost back to today, and divide by the discounted electricity exported over the same years. Subtract pumping and auxiliary power from generation first, because the plant consumes them itself.

### How much does a geothermal well cost?

It depends on depth, rock and temperature, and few operators publish their costs. The US Department of Energy says casing and cementing make up 30% to 40% or more of a well's cost. Our model treats the whole subsurface scope as an allowance of $15m, $25m or $37m per case. Those are assumptions for comparison, and no contractor has quoted them.

### Is there a free geothermal LCOE calculator?

Yes. The Zemanium power-cost model at zemanium.com/confidence runs in a browser and needs no account. For full reservoir and plant simulation, GEOPHIRES-X is open source.

### Why does the discount rate matter so much for geothermal?

Nearly all the money is spent before the first megawatt-hour is sold, so the financing cost applies to almost the whole budget. In our simulated example the same plant costs $43.35 per megawatt-hour at an 8% real discount rate and $35.00 at 4%.

# Geothermal stocks in 2026: the listed producers and what their plants deliver.

The two US-listed companies that run mainly on geothermal power are Ormat Technologies (NYSE: ORA), the largest, and Fervo Energy (Nasdaq: FRVO), listed in May 2026. Six more listed companies in Indonesia, Kenya, New Zealand and Canada own large geothermal fleets. Below is each one, its capacity from its own reports, and the public plant record behind the numbers.

Capacity figures are company statements. Nevada output figures are measured and operator-reported to the state regulator. Independent analysis from public records; not investment advice. Zemanium holds no position in any security.

01 / Companies

## Which geothermal companies are publicly traded?

Eight listed companies own large geothermal fleets. The table gives each one's exchange, ticker and capacity as the company reports it.

| Company | Ticker | Geothermal position | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Ormat Technologies** | NYSE: ORA | 1,853 MW generating portfolio, of which 1,358 MW geothermal and solar generation | company, 4 Nov 2026 [[1]](https://zemanium.com/guides/geothermal-stocks#s1) |
| **Fervo Energy** | Nasdaq: FRVO | Enhanced geothermal developer; listed May 2026; Cape Station, Utah, first power 24 Sep 2026 from a first unit of about 33 MW; 900 MW contracted | company, 24 Sep 2026 [[3]](https://zemanium.com/guides/geothermal-stocks#s3) |
| **Pertamina Geothermal Energy** | IDX: PGEO | 1,932 MW installed in Indonesia, of which 727 MW operated on its own and 1,205 MW with partners | company, Q2 2025 [[4]](https://zemanium.com/guides/geothermal-stocks#s4) |
| **Barito Renewables (Star Energy Geothermal)** | IDX: BREN | 935.55 MW at Salak, Darajat and Wayang Windu, Indonesia | company, 2026 [[5]](https://zemanium.com/guides/geothermal-stocks#s5) |
| **KenGen** | NSE: KEGN | 754 MW of geothermal in a 1,786 MW fleet, mostly at Olkaria, Kenya | company, year to June 2025 [[6]](https://zemanium.com/guides/geothermal-stocks#s6) |

Large utilities such as Enel and Berkshire Hathaway Energy also own geothermal plants, where geothermal is a small share of the business. Drilling and equipment suppliers such as SLB, Halliburton and Baker Hughes earn part of their revenue from geothermal wells.

02 / Fervo

## Fervo Energy (FRVO): what the public record shows.

Fervo priced its initial public offering at $27 a share on 12 May 2026 and sold 70 million shares; trading on Nasdaq began on 13 May. Its first commercial plant, Cape Station in Utah, reached first power on 24 September 2026, with a first phase of about 100 MW planned, by the company's account.

Fervo's pilot well pair, Project Red in Nevada, is the only enhanced geothermal system with a public monthly production record. Its wellhead temperature read 347 °F at its 2024 plateau and 316 °F in July 2026. We track it every month against a forecast registered on 19 November 2026.

[Open the Project Red tracker ](https://zemanium.com/fervo-project-red)

03 / Record

## What Nevada's geothermal plants produced, year by year.

Nevada publishes monthly output for every geothermal plant in the state. Statewide output was 5,044 GWh in 2019, peaked at 5,391 GWh in 2023 and was 5,031 GWh in 2025. The McGinness Hills complex, whose operator of record is Ormat Nevada and its ORNI subsidiaries, is the largest single site in the record.

|---|---|---|

04 / Method

## How to read a geothermal producer.

- **Capacity factor.** Energy produced in a year divided by capacity times 8,760 hours. Geothermal plants run day and night, so a falling figure usually means the wells deliver less heat.
- **Reservoir temperature trend.** A well that cools needs makeup drilling to hold output. The regulator records in Nevada show it field by field.
- **Cost per megawatt-hour.** Our [cost guide](https://zemanium.com/guides/geothermal-electricity-cost) shows which inputs move it, and the [power-cost model](https://zemanium.com/confidence/) prices a plant under your assumptions.

05 / Questions

## Common questions.

### Is Fervo Energy publicly traded?

Yes. Fervo Energy trades on Nasdaq under the ticker FRVO. It priced its initial public offering at $27 a share on 12 May 2026 and began trading on 13 May 2026.

### What is the largest geothermal stock?

By capacity, Pertamina Geothermal Energy (IDX: PGEO) reports 1,932 MW installed including partner-operated plants. Among US-listed companies, Ormat Technologies (NYSE: ORA) is the largest, with a 1,853 MW portfolio that also includes solar and storage.

### Are there geothermal stocks outside the United States?

Yes. Pertamina Geothermal Energy and Barito Renewables trade in Jakarta, KenGen in Nairobi, Mercury NZ and Contact Energy in New Zealand, and Polaris Renewable Energy in Toronto.

### Where can I check a geothermal plant's actual output?

In Nevada, the Division of Minerals publishes monthly output for every plant and monthly temperature for every well. Our Nevada plant file and the Project Red tracker take their numbers from that record. Across the United States, the EIA publishes monthly generation by plant.

# Is geothermal energy renewable? What the field records show.

Yes. Geothermal energy is renewable because the Earth keeps producing heat inside it, as the US Energy Information Administration puts it. A single reservoir can still cool when a plant draws heat faster than the rock refills it, and Nevada's public well records show how fast that happens, field by field.

Field temperatures and plant output are measured and operator-reported to the Nevada Division of Minerals. Flow-weighted means are computed by Zemanium from that record.

01 / Answer

## Is geothermal energy renewable or nonrenewable?

Geothermal energy is renewable. The heat comes from the Earth's interior, which keeps producing it, and power plants send the used water back underground. The EIA classes it as a renewable source on that basis.

The heat in one reservoir refills slowly, over decades to centuries. So a field can be renewable as a resource while a given well pair cools during its working life. Operators manage that with spacing, injection and new wells.

02 / Mechanism

## How does geothermal energy work?

1. Wells reach hot water or hot rock deep underground.
2. Hot water or steam rises to the surface and drives a turbine, directly or through a second fluid in a binary plant.
3. The cooled water goes back down an injection well and heats up again in the rock.

Because nothing burns and the loop runs in any weather, a geothermal plant delivers power around the clock. [Enhanced geothermal systems](https://zemanium.com/guides/enhanced-geothermal-systems) build the same loop in hot rock that has no natural water or cracks.

03 / Record

## What Nevada's field records show.

Nevada publishes the monthly temperature of every producing geothermal well. Across 18 fields with ten or more years of record and production in 2025, the flow-weighted mean temperature fell by more than 5 °F in 11, stayed within 5 °F in 3 and rose in 4. Statewide geothermal output was 5,044 GWh in 2019 and 5,031 GWh in 2025.

| Field (regulator code) | First year | First-year mean | 2025 mean | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Blue Mountain (BLU) | 2009 | 368 °F | 281 °F | -87 °F |
| WRS2 (WRS2) | 2015 | 261 °F | 212 °F | -49 °F |
| Jersey Valley (JVP) | 2012 | 331 °F | 292 °F | -38 °F |
| WRS (WRS) | 2013 | 260 °F | 227 °F | -32 °F |
| Brady Hot Springs (BHS) | 2012 | 280 °F | 248 °F | -32 °F |
| McGinness Hills 2 (MGH2) | 2015 | 336 °F | 307 °F | -29 °F |
| McGinness Hills (MGH) | 2012 | 335 °F | 306 °F | -29 °F |
| Tuscarora (TUS) | 2012 | 341 °F | 313 °F | -28 °F |
| Salt Wells (SWL) | 2009 | 276 °F | 248 °F | -28 °F |
| Steamboat (STB) | 2012 | 290 °F | 263 °F | -27 °F |
| Patua (PTA) | 2013 | 303 °F | 293 °F | -10 °F |
| Soda Lake (SDL) | 2012 | 329 °F | 325 °F | -4 °F |
| Dixie Valley (DXV) | 2012 | 330 °F | 330 °F | -1 °F |
| Wabuska (WAB) | 2012 | 209 °F | 209 °F | +0 °F |
| Desert Peak (DPK) | 2012 | 295 °F | 302 °F | +7 °F |
| San Emidio (SEM) | 2012 | 284 °F | 300 °F | +16 °F |
| Stillwater (STW) | 2009 | 270 °F | 297 °F | +27 °F |
| Beowawe (BEO) | 2012 | 274 °F | 324 °F | +50 °F |

A field's mean also moves when operators add or retire wells, so this table shows the produced fluid, not the rock alone. The yearly values for every field are in [one JSON file](https://zemanium.com/data/nevada-field-temperature.json), CC BY 4.0.

The clearest single well-pair record is Fervo's Project Red, which went from a 347 °F plateau in 2024 to 316 °F in July 2026. [See the monthly tracker](https://zemanium.com/fervo-project-red).

04 / Practice

## How operators keep a geothermal field hot.

- **Reinjection.** Sending the used water back keeps reservoir pressure up and returns the fluid for reheating. Most plants reinject, according to the EIA.
- **Well spacing.** Injection wells placed far enough from producers give the water more rock to heat it before it returns.
- **Makeup wells.** When a well cools, operators drill a new one into hotter rock nearby.
- **Even flow.** In enhanced systems, spreading flow across many fractures uses more rock and slows cooling. Our [reservoir explorer](https://zemanium.com/demo/) shows the effect.

05 / Trade-offs

## Geothermal energy pros and cons.

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Runs day and night in any weather | Good conventional sites are limited to hot regions |
| About 99% less carbon dioxide than fossil plants, per the EIA | Drilling is expensive and dominates the cost |
| Most plants send their water back underground, per the EIA | Single reservoirs can cool over a plant's life |
| Fuel cost is zero | Stimulation can trigger small earthquakes |

Our [cost guide](https://zemanium.com/guides/geothermal-electricity-cost) shows what geothermal electricity costs per megawatt-hour and which inputs move it.

06 / Questions

## Common questions.

### Why is geothermal energy considered renewable?

Because the Earth keeps producing heat in its interior, and power plants return the used water underground to be heated again. The US Energy Information Administration lists geothermal as a renewable energy source.

### Can a geothermal reservoir run out?

A reservoir can cool if heat is drawn out faster than the surrounding rock replaces it. In Nevada's records, 11 of 18 long-running fields produced cooler fluid in 2025 than in their first recorded year, and operators drill makeup wells to hold output.

### Is geothermal energy clean?

Geothermal plants burn no fuel. The EIA reports about 97% less sulfur compounds and about 99% less carbon dioxide than fossil fuel plants, and plants use scrubbers to remove hydrogen sulfide.

### How long does a geothermal power plant last?

Plants commonly run for decades, with wells replaced or added as fields cool. Our cost model assumes a 25-year life for a new plant.

Guide · Toni Zemani · 20 November 2026

# Superhot rock geothermal: what happens above 375 °C.

Superhot rock geothermal means producing heat from rock hotter than about 375 °C at pressures above 22 MPa. Water there is supercritical, and the US Department of Energy says it can deliver several times the power density of cooler rock. Two research wells in Iceland have met fluid hotter than 400 °C, and both were damaged.

Every figure below is quoted from the source listed beside it. Targets are labelled as targets.

01 / In brief

## The short answer.

- The threshold is the critical point of water, about 374 °C and 22.1 MPa. ARPA-E and the US Department of Energy both define superhot as above 375 °C.
- ARPA-E expects a superhot well to produce up to 30 to 50 megawatts of electricity, against about 10 for an enhanced geothermal well today.
- Iceland's IDDP-1 well flowed steam at 450 °C and suffered acid corrosion and silica erosion. IDDP-2 logged 426 °C at about 4,550 m and its casing was damaged.
- Wells fail through their steel, cement and instruments. Casing breaks when the well is heated and cooled, and electronics stop working near 225 °C.

02 / Motive

## Why go hotter.

Each well is expensive, so power per well drives the price of electricity. ARPA-E says current equipment holds enhanced geothermal to about 220 °C and about 10 megawatts of electricity per production well, and that superhot reservoirs could raise this to 30 to 50. Its SUPERHOT program aims at 10 to 20 GW of baseload power at under $30 per megawatt-hour by 2040.

Other estimates of output per well exist. A 2022 study by LucidCatalyst and HERO for the Clean Air Task Force modelled 17 to 29 MW per production well at 55 kg/s. Iceland's power company Orkuveitan is targeting 20 to 50 MW from one well in the IDDP-3 project, and says it has not demonstrated that figure. Conventional wells there make 2 to 7 MW.

03 / Record

## Wells drilled so far.

| Well | What was measured | What went wrong |
|---|---|---|
| IDDP-1, Krafla, Iceland | superheated steam at 450 °C and 140 bar at the wellhead | condensed steam carried hydrochloric and hydrofluoric acid; silica eroded surface equipment when wellhead pressure fell below 80 bar; repeated shutdowns increased corrosion |
| IDDP-2, Reykjanes, Iceland | 426 °C at 340 bar logged at about 4,550 m; about 600 °C inferred at the bottom | production casing damaged between 2,307 and 2,380 m, presumably by cyclic heating and cooling |
| Newberry, Oregon (Mazama Energy) | 331 °C in October 2025; a later well above 700 °F | none reported |

At IDDP-2 the logging tools stayed below 65 °C in rock hotter than 400 to 500 °C for as long as cold water circulated. The production casing was damaged all the same, presumably by repeated heating and cooling.

Next in line: IDDP-3 in Iceland is planned in four stages from late 2026 to 2028. Quaise Energy's Project Obsidian in Oregon targets a well above 400 °C and first power in 2030. Quaise drills with millimetre waves and had completed a 118 m hole in granite by July 2025.

04 / Limits

## What fails first.

| Component | Published limit | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Casing and couplings | most well failures in a review of 20 high-temperature wells came from thermal stress during quenching or the start of production | Kruszewski and Wittig, 2018 |
| Portland cement with 35% to 40% silica flour | proven where produced fluid stays below 350 °C | Kruszewski and Wittig, 2018 |
| Downhole electronics in service | about 210 to 225 °C | Hephae, 2026; IMAPS HiTEC, 2016 |
| Temperature logging tools | 350 °C for four hours | Kruszewski and Wittig, 2018 |
| Polyimide-coated optical fibre | 300 °C continuously, 350 °C briefly | manufacturer's statement (Exail) |
| Silicon carbide circuits, in the laboratory | one year at 500 °C in air | NASA Glenn, 2018 |
| Casing connection test standard ISO/TS 12835:2022 | written for wells that cycle from well below 180 °C up to maxima of 180 °C to 350 °C or above; covers connections only | ISO |

ARPA-E's program description says conventional steel casing and Portland cement are inadequate for superhot wells, and that well materials have to survive high temperature, rapid temperature change and corrosive fluid for 15 years or more.

05 / Funding

## Who is funding it.

- ARPA-E SUPERHOT announced eight awards on 12 November 2026: Blade Energy Partners ($6.3m), Lawrence Livermore ($5.5m), Los Alamos ($3.5m), University of Oklahoma ($3.1m), Oak Ridge ($3.0m), University of Southern California ($3.0m), XGS Energy ($3.0m) and Pacific Northwest National Laboratory ($2.6m).
- The US Department of Energy is funding a superhot EGS demonstration above 375 °C on the western flank of Newberry Volcano in Oregon.
- Japan's NEDO plans five 100 MW class supercritical geothermal plants around 2040 to 2050 and estimates the resource at 11 GW.
- The European SHiFT consortium received €10m from Horizon Europe for technology above 400 °C.
- Mazama Energy raised $135m in September 2026. Quaise Energy closed a Series B of $180m in August 2026.

06 / Zemanium

## What we are working on.

Our work is on the well itself: how casing and cement behave through heating and cooling cycles above 375 °C, and how to record a test so that someone outside the company can check it. We use gauges that can be bought today. In November 2026 we stopped our own long-line acoustic sensor after it failed a simulation gate we had set in advance; the [record is on the research page](https://zemanium.com/room/#sensing).

We rebuilt IDDP-1's production casing in a model and ran it through the well's recorded history: two discharges, then the kill of July 2012. The video log of 2014 found three couplings pulled apart at 300, 356 and 505 m. In 88 of 128 sampled wells our model reproduces that log (SIMULATED, registered and time-stamped before the run). The string parts first at 292 m, just below the point at 290 m where the outer anchor casing changes size, with gaps inside the logged 250 to 400 mm. Two wellhead readings the model was never fitted to land inside their measured bands. The model is calibrated to one well, and the next run is aimed at the second and third partings.

That replay is the test bench for Pandora, our casing joint for wells at 450 to 500 °C. Pandora is built to carry a string through the same history without parting. Its first metal, a subscale joint, is next.

If you operate, design or finance hot wells and want to compare notes, write to [toni@zemanium.com](mailto:toni@zemanium.com).

07 / Questions

## Common questions.

### What is superhot rock geothermal?

It is geothermal energy from rock hotter than about 375 °C at pressure above 22 MPa, where water becomes supercritical. A well in those conditions can carry several times the energy of a conventional geothermal well.

### How hot is superhot rock?

Above 375 °C by the definitions of ARPA-E and the US Department of Energy. Iceland's IDDP-1 produced steam at 450 °C, and IDDP-2 logged 426 °C with about 600 °C inferred at the bottom of the well.

### Has anyone produced power from superhot rock?

No commercial plant runs on superhot rock yet. IDDP-1 flowed steam at 450 °C and IDDP-2 logged 426 °C at 340 bar, and both wells were damaged. Quaise Energy targets first power in Oregon in 2030, and Japan's NEDO plans plants around 2040 to 2050.

### What is the IDDP?

The Iceland Deep Drilling Project, a research programme run by Icelandic energy companies to drill into supercritical geothermal zones. IDDP-1 was drilled at Krafla, IDDP-2 at Reykjanes, and IDDP-3 is planned from late 2026.

### Why do superhot wells fail?

Mostly from thermal cycling. Steel casing expands when the well heats and contracts when cold water is pumped in, and the stress breaks casing and couplings. A 2018 review of 20 high-temperature wells found that most failures came from thermal stress during quenching or the start of production.

### How much power can one superhot well produce?

ARPA-E expects up to 30 to 50 megawatts of electricity per well, compared with about 10 megawatts for an enhanced geothermal well at 220 °C. That output has not been demonstrated.

Open research · updated 20 November 2026

# Open models, records and drawings.

This page lists everything Zemanium has published, what each item is, and what you may do with it. Use it, check it and build on it.

Model output is labelled SIMULATED, and field data is credited to the parties who measured it.

01 / Models

## Models you can run.

| Item | What it does | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| [Forecast and audit record, Project Red](https://github.com/tonizemani2/forecast-audit) | One command refits a conduction model to the Nevada regulator's monthly record of the first enhanced geothermal well pair, recomputes its water balance, and checks forecasts that were time-stamped on 19 November 2026. The model matches nine steady months to 0.51 °F. Each forecast is scored when the regulator publishes the month. | Model results on measured regulator data; code MIT, text CC BY 4.0; [doi:10.5281/zenodo.24396505](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24396505) |
| [Power-cost model](https://zemanium.com/confidence/) | Computes the cost per megawatt-hour of a geothermal plant from plant cost, subsurface cost and discount rate across 1,080 scenarios, with a 2,000-draw financial stress test. Shows the cases that fail. | SIMULATED, on GEOPHIRES-X 3.18.3 trajectories, 5 October 2026 |
| [Reservoir explorer](https://zemanium.com/demo/) | A 3D reservoir where you change flow, well spacing, permeability and rock temperature and see thermal decline, power and pumping. | SIMULATED, illustrative, earlier design assumptions |
| [Utah FORGE field replay](https://zemanium.com/confidence/#field) | 518 rows of a published production-log interpretation, with the unresolved intervals shown as gaps. | Measured and published by SLB and the University of Utah for Utah FORGE; CC BY 4.0; [doi:10.15121/2473673](https://doi.org/10.15121/2473673) |

06 / Citation

## How to cite.

For a guide: Toni Zemani, title of the guide, Zemanium, date shown on the page, and its address. For a model or record: Zemanium, name of the item, its date, its address, and the label it carries (SIMULATED).

07 / Agents

## For software agents.

[llms.txt](https://zemanium.com/llms.txt) lists every page with a one-line description. [llms-full.txt](https://zemanium.com/llms-full.txt) holds the guides in one Markdown file. Each guide also has a Markdown copy at its own address with `.md` added. The [sitemap](https://zemanium.com/sitemap.xml) lists canonical addresses. Search and AI crawlers are allowed on the whole site, and the same files are mirrored at [github.com/tonizemani2/zemanium-open](https://github.com/tonizemani2/zemanium-open).

08 / Contact

## Work with us.

We publish so that specialists can check the work, and so that people with a problem we can help with can find us. Three kinds of conversation have a clear next step.

| You have | We can |
|---|---|
| A forecast, cost case or test plan you need checked | Review it independently and give you the numbers we reproduce and the ones we cannot |
| A well, tool or material problem above 200 °C | Scope a sponsored experiment with a fixed question, a named engineer and raw results at the end |
| A use for one of the hardware designs | License it, or develop it with you |

Write to [toni@zemanium.com](mailto:toni@zemanium.com) with what you need to decide. Investors and engineers who want to join are welcome at the same address.
